newsitem.title: USA: Atlantis lifts off for rendezvous with Mir.
newsitem.headline: Atlantis lifts off for rendezvous with Mir.

text.p: Shuttle Atlantis blasted off on Monday, headed for space station Mir to pick up U.S. astronaut Shannon Lucid and drop off her replacement.
The $2 billion spaceship, running nearly seven weeks late, roared into the Florida night sky at 4:54 a.m. EDT (0854 GMT), beginning a three-day chase through space to catch the Russian station.
The shuttle's blast off sets the stage for a docking with Mir late on Wednesday.
Lucid, a 53-year-old biochemist, has been aboard the Russian space station since March and was supposed to have returned home aboard Atlantis in early August.
The shuttle's launch, originally scheduled for July 31, was postponed by six weeks because NASA ordered the replacement of its twin rocket boosters, fearing a dangerous flaw in the rocket's joints.

Menacing hurricanes lurking off the Florida coast forced NASA to twice haul the shuttle off its launch pad, delaying it a few more days. And a scheduling clash with an unmanned rocket caused a further delay.
